document.title: Afghanistan: Taleban External Ambitions
document.authors: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Intelligence and Research (INR)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] Despite limited capacity, signs including Mullah Omar's statements after the embassy bombings indicate a broadening of Taliban goals. Under bin Laden's influence the Taliban may expand beyond Afghanistan. Taliban-like movements in Pakistan are already feeling its influence, and Iran fears Sunni cross-border subversion.

key_claims: The Taleban lack the resources and ideological vision to pursue a broad pan-Islamic agenda and remain focused on military victory in Afghanistan.
Taleban willingness to host foreign militant training camps could become a ready-made asset for exporting their revolution.
Taleban control areas with Kashmiri and bin Ladin-associated training camps and, with Pakistani encouragement, protect them.
Mullah Omar's criticism of Saudi Arabia and the US Gulf presence may reflect bin Ladin's influence.
Taleban rise has boosted JUI and further radicalized Pakistani Sunni militants against Shia.
Iran and Central Asian states, notably Tajikistan, fear Taleban-inspired subversion.
